title: Procedural Programming: Modules and State
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: procedure — Named subroutine mainly performing an action.
function — Subroutine that returns a value.
parameter — Named input used by a routine.
scope — Region where an identifier may be accessed.

blocks.title: Sequence and control
blocks.text: Statements execute in an order; selection and loops direct flow.

blocks.title: Procedure/function
blocks.text: Reusable named routines accept parameters; functions return values.

blocks.title: Scope and state
blocks.text: Local variables limit unwanted side effects; global state needs care.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model answer
blocks.text: Parameter x=4, local result=8, return value 9, printed output 9. The local result does not become a global variable merely because the function runs. Check: link each claim to the scenario and use precise OCR terminology.

blocks.text: Arguments bind w=3 and h=5; return 15; print shows 15. A procedure is intended primarily to perform an action rather than return a result (conventions vary by language).
